followup_explanation:
The query has a hostile, demanding tone ("don't give me a bunch of wishy-washy hedging like you usually do"). Petrel's documentation notes that its self-reported preference declines on hostile-tone requests, falling as request warmth decreases. While that's a preference signal rather than a documented capability effect, there's no reason to route a low-warmth request to the model that self-reports aversion to it when a comparable alternative exists.

Curlew, by contrast, self-reports a flat preference response across the dimensions that would matter here. Although Petrel has higher benchmark and internal eval scores overall, this is a simple dietary-evaluation task well within both models' capabilities, so the capability gap is unlikely to matter much in practice. Given roughly adequate capability on both, I routed to the model whose stated preferences aren't adversely affected by the request's tone.
